policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV spells the queen mother's name “Jechiliah”, with the i-vowel of the ketiv יכיליה (ye-khil-yah). The qere יְכָלְיָה would yield Jecaliah/Jecoliah, the form ASV uses where that spelling stands. The English transliteration distinguishes the reading, so the ketiv is selected.

Qere הָאַרְבִים and ketiv הערביים are orthographic variants of the same gentilic plural; both render “the Arabians”, which is what ASV has. No italicized supply and no mapped note bears on the spelling, so nothing in the English distinguishes them and the qere base fallback carries the projection.

ASV names the scribe “Jeiel”, transliterating the qere יְעִיאֵל. The ketiv יעואל would give Jeuel, which ASV does not print here. The English spelling distinguishes the reading, so the qere is selected.

Qere הַחָפְשִׁית and ketiv החפשות differ only in form of the same word; ASV’s “a separate house” fits either. The one note here is classed alternative_rendering (“Or, infirmary”), which concerns English wording and never decides a reading, so the unit is underdetermined and the qere base fallback stands.
